note: Every backend/src/**/*.ts arithmetic site this ratchet finds outside *.spec.ts/*.db-spec.ts. AS OF 2026-09-18: 40 keys, 44 occurrences — a COUNT CORRECTION, not a re-audit. This header said "29 keys, 32 occurrences" from 2026-09-15 until 2026-09-18 while the file itself grew past it (dev-seed.history.ts's nine entries and crate-code.ts's arrived in between), because nothing pins this sentence: the ratchet compares the ENTRIES against the tree and never reads this note, and registry.test.mjs pins counts in registry.mjs, not here. The 2026-09-18 pass re-keyed four dev-seed.ts entries for line drift and corrected this number; it did NOT re-read all 40 reasons at their sites, so every reason below still carries its own original date and stands on that reading, not on this one. THE SCOPE WIDENED ON 2026-09-15 and the count did not move: until then this ratchet skipped the four module trees backend/eslint.config.mjs policed when it was written (src/intakes/, src/payouts/, src/shifts/, src/supplier-balance/). eslint's own `files` list had since grown to eight trees while this ratchet's hard-coded copy of it had not, so the two scopes silently disagreed — and a tree DELETED from eslint's list would have been policed by neither. Scanning all of backend/src was measured before the carve-out was removed: exactly zero additional findings, because eslint's ban is what keeps those trees clean. Read individually before writing a reason, not inferred from the shape of the code. Four of the 29 keys are backend/src/common/money.ts's OWN internals (the *, /, and mul()'s two / occurrences on one line) — the money engine works in bigint, not JS number, so it carries none of the float-precision risk this ratchet exists to catch, but the AST heuristic only recognises number-typed or numeric-literal operands, not bigint-safety, so those sites are listed honestly here rather than exempted by widening the rule's path exclusions. Three keys (backend/src/seed/dev-seed.ts:59 and :66) are a genuine concern, not a false positive: the dev seed script reimplements money.ts's add() independently, through Number() and plain-number division, to compute real values written into grade_prices.base_price for the seeded demo dataset — a real duplicate of the one authorised rounding seam, left as-is because backend/src is out of scope for the verify layer. Two keys (password-hashing.ts:28's two occurrences) are literal-and-number-typed arithmetic that this rule's single-level operand check cannot prove clear because each is the OUTER multiplication of a left-associative a*b*c chain, whose left operand is itself a BinaryExpression rather than a bare literal or identifier. Every remaining key is one of two shapes: the repeated (page - 1) * limit pagination-offset arithmetic this template's list endpoints all share (10 keys, including pagination-query.dto.ts's own skipOf() helper), or an env-var/config integer parsed with Number()/parseInt() (ports, throttle window/limit) or Math.min() retry-backoff arithmetic that is never a monetary or weight value. None were left unclassified — every entry's reason states what the arithmetic actually is, read at its site. Five entries were RE-KEYED on 2026-09-15 rather than added: all five are sites this file already carried, whose line numbers moved under main's merge. This ratchet is two-directional: a new site not listed here fails scripts/verify/ratchets/money-rounding.mjs, and a listed entry whose site (or exact occurrence count) no longer matches the tree fails it too — this file may only shrink or be re-dated by a reviewed change, never grow by drift.

money.ts's own allocate(): (magnitude * w) inside the per-line floor of a largest-remainder split. Bigint kopiykas times a bigint weight, never a JS number. The whole point of allocate() is that the parts sum EXACTLY to the total — §8.4's звірка checks precisely that on screen — which is why the split is done here rather than by multiplying each line by a pre-rounded ratio, the approach that drifts a kopiyka per line. money.ts's own allocate(): (magnitude * w) / basisTotal, the floor of each line's pro-rata share. Bigint division truncates, which is deliberate here — the truncated remainders are what the largest-remainder loop below then distributes, so nothing is lost and nothing is invented. Added 2026-09-18 with the reweigh slice. RE-KEYED 2026-09-18 (:158 -> :161) by the §8.3–8.6 cost-of-day slice stacked on the reweigh one: Same three-line comment correction in div() above allocate(). money.ts's own mul(): parse(a) * parse(b), the scale-4 bigint product before mul() rounds it back to scale 2 half-up. This IS the rounding engine itself — §2.7's amount calculation runs through exactly this line — audited by money.spec.ts, not by this AST heuristic.

maxmemFor()'s own body: Math.max(32 * 1024 * 1024, 256 * n * r) computes scrypt's maxmem option in bytes from the cost parameters N and r. Each inner multiplication (32 * 1024, 256 * n) clears on its own since every operand is a number-typed identifier or a numeric literal, but this rule inspects only a BinaryExpression's two immediate operands, so the OUTER multiplication in each left-associative chain ((32 * 1024) * 1024 and (256 * n) * r) sees a nested BinaryExpression as its left operand and is not provably cleared by this single-level heuristic. This is scrypt memory sizing, not money or weight.
const n = Number(rawN) — parses the scrypt cost parameter N back out of the self-describing stored-hash format (scrypt$N$r$p$salt$hash); a cost parameter, not money.
const r = Number(rawR) — same stored-hash format, the scrypt cost parameter r; not money.
const p = Number(rawP) — same stored-hash format, the scrypt cost parameter p; not money.
